name: Proofreading Checklist
description: This module is a pre-completion checklist for proofreading work: a short set of checks to run before calling a proofreading task done.
content:
This module is a pre-completion checklist for proofreading work: a short set of checks to run before calling a proofreading task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Validate proofreading outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
2. Measure before optimizing any proofreading bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. Prefer explicit, readable proofreading solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
4. Surface known limitations of a chosen proofreading approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
5. When proofreading decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to proofreading (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Document any non-obvious proofreading decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop proofreading edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid introducing new proofreading abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of proofreading correctness.
- Do not apply generic proofreading advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid mixing unrelated proofreading concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about proofreading over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
